newsitem.title: USA: ARCO expects 4 pct/yr production growth.
newsitem.headline: ARCO expects 4 pct/yr production growth.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co expects average annual growth of more than 4 percent in its worldwide oil and gas production over the next five years, chief executive Mike R. Bowlin said Thursday.

"This growth will come from identified projects in the U.S. and overseas. Our worldwide reserve replacement will exceed 120% per year, on average, from 1997-2001. Total international reserves will more than double by the year 2000," Bowlin told security analysts.
Based on identified opportunities, ARCO's 1997-2001 capital spending plan has grown to $19 billion.

That is up from $14 billion projected for the previous five-year period, Bowlin said. Included is planned spending of $12 billion in the upstream oil and gas business and $7 billion in downstream refining, marketing and chemicals.
"I want to exceed our previously announced goal of $2 billion in net income in 2000," he said, "and I want our stock price to be at least $100 per share on a post-split basis."

He said ARCO expects to book just under 100 million barrels of oil equivalent this year related to its 27.5 percent interest in the North Sea Shearwater project approved last week by the British government.

In Indonesia, ARCO is continuing delineation of its large Weriagar discovery in Irian Jaya. ARCO expects to certify 6 to 7 trillion cubic feet of reserves in Irian Jaya, sufficient for a two-train liquefied natural gas project starting up in the next decade.

Bowlin said ARCO's optimism over its Alaska production profile, which now shows "No Decline After '99," has increased. Production will stabilize at 50,000 barrels per day higher than ARCO estimated last year.
Most of Alaska's improved production outlook comes from known oil accumulations on the North Slope.
This includes the Alpine field development announced in 1996, the Tarn field discovery announced in March, and initial development of the West Sak oil field.
For the longer term, ARCO's Alaska unit continues to work with partners in the Prudhoe Bay field and the State of Alaska to pursue an economically feasible North Slope liquefied natural gas project.
He said the company also has aggressive growth plans in its downstream core businesses:

-- ARCO is committed to remaining the No. 1 gasoline marketer on the West Coast. It will add 265 new sites to its base network over the next five years, in addition to about 260 new California sites being leased from Thrifty Oil Co.

-- ARCO plans to build the only polypropylene facility in the Western United States. The worldscale plant, to be constructed at ARCO's Los Angeles Refinery, should be operational by the first quarter of 1999.
